title: Korea Stock Market Today, Oct 13, 2026: KOSPI -5.46% on China Memory Fears
content:
KOSPI closed at 6,035.35, down 5.46%, holding just above the 6,000 level, and KOSDAQ closed at 837.03, down 1.43%, as worries that China's CXMT is catching up in memory chips combined with heavy foreign selling. Individual themes still moved on their own news: hopes for a southern Honam semiconductor cluster, continued cybersecurity buying after financial-sector data leaks, and selective strength in KOSDAQ chip equipment and materials.

1. China memory catch-up worries and foreign selling — KOSPI plunges over 5%

After the previous day's sharp drop, news of CXMT's plans for a next-generation server DRAM and its improving technology revived worries about tougher competition for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Caution about the profitability of AI infrastructure investment and weakness in U.S. chip stocks added to heavy foreign selling, and large chip stocks led by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell sharply. KOSPI dropped as low as about 5,911 intraday, below the 6,000 level, and a sell-side sidecar suspending program sell orders was reportedly triggered during the slide. KOSPI closed at 6,035.35 (-5.46%) and KOSDAQ at 837.03 (-1.43%).

2. SK chairman reaffirms a fast pace for the Honam chip cluster — regional stocks rise

Stocks tied to the Honam semiconductor cluster kept rising against the market. SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won dismissed talk that the investment had been withdrawn and said the project would move as fast as possible, and the industry minister visited the planned Gwangju military airport site to check infrastructure such as land, power and water, keeping expectations alive. Seosan rose again after hitting its upper limit the day before, and buying continued in Gwangju- and Jeonnam-based names such as Kumho Electric and Kumho Engineering & Construction.

3. AI hacking at financial firms — cybersecurity spending hopes continue

Large data leaks and suspected hacking at financial companies kept expectations alive for stronger security reviews and more cybersecurity spending. Financial regulators confirmed that data on about 70,000 people was leaked at seven financial companies, and talk that AI may have been used in the attacks raised hopes for upgraded security systems and AI-based threat detection. AhnLab, Raon Secure and Sands Lab were in focus, and buying has recently spread to Genians, ICTK, Fasoo, Xgate and Hancom WITH.

4. Big memory stocks fall — selective strength in KOSDAQ chip equipment

The most notable feature of the chip trade was that large memory stocks such as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell on CXMT competition worries while some chip equipment and materials names saw dip buying and selective inflows. Foreign investors bought some KOSDAQ chip equipment and materials stocks even as they were heavy net sellers on KOSPI, and Jusung Engineering swung from about -4% to about +4% intraday.

Continued global AI infrastructure investment and expectations for Samsung and SK Hynix capital spending support a view that equipment, back-end, test and materials companies can keep winning orders regardless of memory price competition, which underpinned the relative strength of these names. STI, Semi-TS, PSK Holdings, Doosan Tesna, Intekplus, TSE, Macus, PSK and TEMC were in focus. KOSDAQ's market-cap weighting has also been shifting from bio toward chip equipment names such as PSK Holdings, TSE, TES, Simmtech and Leeno Industrial.

Quick FAQ

Why did KOSPI fall more than 5% on Oct 13?
News of CXMT's next-generation server DRAM raised worries about competition for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, and caution about AI investment profitability and weak U.S. chip stocks added to heavy foreign selling. KOSPI closed at 6,035.35 (-5.46%).

Why did KOSDAQ fall much less than KOSPI?
KOSDAQ closed at 837.03 (-1.43%) because dip buying and selective inflows went into chip equipment, materials and test names while large memory stocks fell.

Is the Honam semiconductor cluster confirmed?
No. SK's chairman reaffirmed a fast pace and the industry minister inspected the planned site, but industrial complex designation and company recruitment are still ahead.
